There's no reason the Electoral College has to work that way. Most states choose a winner-take-all system, but there's nothing stopping them from using proportional representation (Maine and Nebraska already do). The problem is that if California does it and Texas doesn't, it will grant an unfair advantage to the Republican Party, because they will receive a portion of California's votes and all of Texas's. Any reform would have to affect all states equally.

If you're interested in actually addressing this issue, you can try to get your state legislature to join the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact. Enacting instant-runoff voting would also be a huge improvement to the status quo, but change frightens most legislators and would make it more difficult to be re-elected, so it's an uphill battle.
